topic: Tension headaches and a tight upper back

slides.headline: Headaches that start in your upper back
slides.sub: Why tension headaches and a tight upper back often turn up together.

slides.title: Why the two often go together
slides.body: Tension-type headaches are often described as a band or pressure around the head. Many people also notice tight, tender muscles across the shoulders, upper back and base of the skull when they flare.

slides.title: Move your upper back every hour
slides.body: Long stretches at a desk tend to stiffen the upper back. Sit tall, hands on shoulders, and slowly rotate side to side ten times. Small, regular movement usually beats one big stretch.

slides.title: Check the usual triggers
slides.body: Poor sleep, stress, skipped meals, dehydration and long screen sessions are common contributors. A simple headache diary for two weeks can help you spot patterns you can actually change.

slides.title: Where chiropractic care fits
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess your neck and upper back, may use adjustments or soft tissue work to ease stiffness, and pair that with exercises and habit changes so you're not relying on hands-on care.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: See your GP promptly for a sudden, severe headache, one after a knock to the head, headaches with fever, confusion, vision changes, weakness or numbness, or a new pattern that keeps getting worse.

slides.headline: Want a plan for your headaches?
slides.body: Book an assessment with our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy. We'll look at your neck, upper back and daily habits, and give you a simple routine to start.
